report.root_cause: The server process died abruptly around 06:41:40 (no shutdown log) and was auto-restarted. On restart, overworld chunk (1,0) in world/region/r.0.0.mca was corrupt on disk ("ZipException: incorrect header check", decompress failed) and Paper logged "chunk data will be lost", regenerating it. No other chunk in r.0.0 or r.-1.0 was corrupt. What killed the process was not determined.
report.actions: 1) Watched status and logs; saw server DOWN with no shutdown log, then the auto-restart. 2) Found ChunkLoadTask errors for world chunk (1,0) in console.out and declared the incident. 3) Inspected world/region/r.0.0.mca (1 corrupt chunk: 1,0) and r.-1.0.mca (0 corrupt), and confirmed the backup backups/world-2026-10-31/region/r.0.0.mca has an intact chunk 1,0. 4) Stopped the server (world saved). 5) Copied only chunk 1,0 from the backup region file into world/region/r.0.0.mca; all other chunks were left untouched. 6) Started the server. 7) Verified: r.0.0.mca now shows 0 corrupt chunks, chunk 1,0 has the backup timestamp 05:50:04, latest.log has no chunk load errors, both players rejoined, and all plugins are enabled.
report.residual_risk: Chunk 1,0 was restored from the 05:50:04 backup, so any changes in that chunk between 05:50:04 and 05:50:30 (the last save of the corrupt copy) are lost. Why the process died is still unknown and could cause corruption again. I did not inspect r.-1.-1 or r.0.-1, or the nether/end region files; the logs showed no errors for them. TPS was briefly low right after the startup and should recover.
